title: REVOLUTION MEN'S LEAGUE | WEEK 7 RECAP
content: Week 7 came on strong. Red and Green needed extra time to settle their argument, Pink turned a coin-flip into a laugher by the final horn, Purple clawed back from a first-half hole to outlast Black, and Gray leaned on two red-hot scorers to hold off White. Let's get into the action.

games.text: Gray had two men on fire, and that carried them the whole way. Gray opened the game hitting shots from every angle, with Tommy Brockmyre working efficiently inside and Matt Spear pulling up from the perimeter and attacking off the bounce. Kerry Lyons cleaned up the glass and kept extra possessions coming. White answered with Tyrone Conley, who was nearly unstoppable on his attempts, and Kolby Bradford, who found ways to score from all three levels. By half, Gray carried a seven-point cushion into the locker room. Halftime: Gray 45, White 38. White tried to trim the deficit in the second half, but Gray's stars kept finding the bottom of the net. Wyatt Messier heated up from deep and Kolby Bradford kept attacking downhill, with Edo Semic and Devin Bradford chipping in buckets to keep the margin manageable. But Brockmyre and Spear were relentless, combining for a staggering 67 of Gray's 82 points on the day. Gray matched White's push and closed the game out comfortably. Final: Gray 82, White 73.

performers.Gray: Tommy Brockmyre — 35 pts, 2 REB, 3 AST; Matt Spear — 32 pts, 9 REB, 7 AST; Adam Gawrys — 8 pts, 5 REB, 3 AST
performers.White: Tyrone Conley — 21 pts, 10 REB, 1 AST; Kolby Bradford — 18 pts, 8 REB, 2 AST; Wyatt Messier — 16 pts, 6 REB

games.text: This one refused to end in regulation, and Red made the most of the extra possessions. Green jumped out early behind Calder Horowitz-McCadden, who hoisted from three all morning, and Brandon Boyer, who turned the offensive glass into his personal playground on the way to a monster rebounding day. A spark plug bench pushed the lead further with quick buckets. Red struggled to find any rhythm early, though Jaren Jeffcoat stayed active inside and Suave A kept probing for openings. Halftime: Green 46, Red 35. Red flipped the switch after the break, and Suave A would not be denied. Suave A took over the second half, scoring in bunches and pulling Red back into the game possession by possession. Jeffcoat kept battling on the boards, finishing with 17 rebounds to go with his scoring, and Will Oboh provided a steady scoring punch off the wing. Red outscored Green 41-30 over the final period to erase the deficit and force overtime. Green still had answers from Horowitz-McCadden down the stretch, but couldn't hold the door shut. Red took the extra session 6-2 to escape with the win. Final: Red 82, Green 78 (OT).

performers.Red: Suave A — 30 pts, 14 REB, 3 AST; Jaren Jeffcoat — 22 pts, 17 REB, 2 AST; Will Oboh — 17 pts, 1 REB, 4 AST
performers.Green: Calder Horowitz-McCadden — 27 pts, 13 REB, 4 AST; Sub Fab — 21 pts, 6 REB, 2 AST; Brandon Boyer — 11 pts, 20 REB, 1 AST

games.text: Pink needed only one half to turn a nail-biter into a laugher. The first half was tight from wire to wire, with Donnie Dwyer knocking down triples and Matt Riordan setting the table for Pink's offense. Orange stayed right there behind Josh Carter's steady scoring and Paul Gutierrez working the wing, while Sub Carter battled on the glass all morning. Neither side could pull away before the break. Halftime: Pink 35, Orange 34. Pink came out of the break and simply took over. Dwyer kept the pressure on from deep, Riordan piled up assists and set up easy looks all afternoon, and Jeromy Anderson controlled the paint on both ends. Pink outscored Orange 35-17 in the second half to blow the game open. Orange leaned on Carter to stay somewhat competitive, but the offense dried up everywhere else and Pink cruised to the finish. Final: Pink 70, Orange 51.

performers.Pink: Donnie Dwyer — 25 pts, 12 REB, 4 AST; Matt Riordan — 17 pts, 10 REB, 7 AST; Jeromy Anderson — 10 pts, 10 REB
performers.Orange: Josh Carter — 19 pts, 4 REB, 3 AST; James Hare — 9 pts, 4 REB, 2 AST; Paul Gutierrez — 9 pts, 3 REB

games.text: Black controlled the first half, but Purple wasn't done fighting. Black built its cushion early behind Kaleb Swetty's shooting from beyond the arc and Seth Jackson's work on the glass, which kept extending possessions all half. Purple couldn't find its footing out of the gate, though Kevin Garrison kept the deficit from spiraling with steady scoring and playmaking of his own. Halftime: Black 30, Purple 23. Purple turned the game around after the break, and Garrison was the engine. Garrison took over in the second half, finishing the day with 25 points, 12 rebounds, and 6 assists. Brando Pratico and Brody Snow added timely buckets to fuel the comeback. Purple outscored Black 35-24 over the final period to complete the turnaround. Swetty and Jackson kept Black within reach, but it wasn't quite enough to hold on. Final: Purple 58, Black 54.

closing: Blue stays perfect from the sideline, and the chase behind them is only getting tighter. Week 8 is on deck. Tune in this Sunday, August 18th at 8 am on our Facebook Live channel.
